fdroid:com.nfcarchiver.cimbar.name: CimBar Scanner
fdroid:com.nfcarchiver.cimbar.summary: Send and receive files and text as animated color barcodes — offline
fdroid:com.nfcarchiver.cimbar.description:
CimBar Scanner sends and receives files and text as CimBar barcodes — animated images in which every frame is a grid of colored tile shapes. Point one phone's camera at another phone's screen, or at a computer running the web app, and the file arrives with no network at all. Encoding and decoding happen entirely on your device: no account, no server, no internet connection.
 How it works 
1. Encode a file or a text message into a CimBar barcode: in the app's Send tab, or with the free web app at https://nfcarchiver.com/cimbar/, which runs entirely in your browser.
2. Show the barcode full screen, or send it as an animated GIF.
3. Receive it with CimBar Scanner: live-scan an animated barcode with the camera, take a photo of a single-frame one, or import the GIF.
4. Open, save or share the recovered file, or copy a received text.
 Features 
• Send tab: type a message or pick a file, add an optional passphrase, then show the barcode full screen — the screen stays on and bright, and repair frames keep coming for as long as it is shown — or share it as an animated GIF
• Received text messages appear right in the app, ready to copy, share or save as .txt
• Live scan with focus and exposure lock, an aiming guide, and hints such as "move closer" or "hold still"
• Frames can be caught in any order: extra repair frames mean any N frames of an N-frame barcode complete the file, so there is no waiting for the one frame you missed
• In-app photo or gallery image for single-frame barcodes
• Import CimBar GIFs from your files, or share one to the app from any other app, such as your gallery; a shared photo of a single-frame barcode goes straight to the photo decoder
• Reed-Solomon error correction in every frame
• Automatic decompression of files that were compressed on encoding
• Optional AES-256-GCM encryption, detected automatically; if a live scan turns out to be encrypted, enter the passphrase right there — no rescan
• Decoded files: open them in another app, save them to Downloads or any folder, or share them
• 7 languages: English, Russian, Ukrainian, Turkish, Georgian, Polish, Belarusian
 Privacy 
No data collection, no analytics, no trackers, no ads. The only permission the app requests is the camera, used for scanning; no internet access.
 Open source 
CimBar Scanner is inspired by libcimbar and CFC by sz3 (https://github.com/sz3/libcimbar), the original Color Icon Matrix Barcode projects, but it is a separate project, not an official cimbar app. It uses its own format, CimBar-XL, so it does not read barcodes made by libcimbar or CFC.
MIT licensed. Source code, format specification and the web encoder: https://github.com/mezinster/cimbar

fdroid:io.github.mgdx.sceau.name: Sceau
fdroid:io.github.mgdx.sceau.summary: Reads and verifies the chip of passports and ID cards, fully offline
fdroid:io.github.mgdx.sceau.description:
Sceau reads the chip of ICAO 9303 identity documents over NFC and checks that they are genuine. It works entirely offline: no network permission, nothing is kept, nothing is sent.
 Supported documents 
 Biometric passports from any country, using the document number, date of birth and expiry date
 French national identity card (credit card format, since 2021), using the 6-digit CAN printed on the card
 European identity cards, using the CAN or the MRZ
 What Sceau shows 
 The photo stored in the chip
 Identity: surname, given names, sex, date of birth, nationality, document number, issuing state, expiry date
 The holder's handwritten signature, if the issuing state stored it in the chip
 Additional data when the chip holds it (place of birth, address, issuing authority and date of issue…)
 What Sceau verifies 
 The issuing state's signature over the data, up to a known root certificate, and the integrity of each data group (Passive Authentication)
 That the chip is not a clone, when the document supports it (Chip Authentication, Active Authentication)
The result is a verdict (Authentic, Valid signature but chip not verified, Unknown issuer, Failed) with a detailed checklist.
 Trust store 
Sceau ships the French CSCA certificates published by ANTS, certificates published by the United Kingdom, Georgia and Luxembourg for their own documents, and the German Master List published by BSI, which covers the European Union, the EEA, Switzerland and the United Kingdom among others. The trust store screen can be searched by country. For a document whose issuer is not included, the verdict is "Unknown issuer"; you can import a Master List published by another state, or a single CSCA or link certificate after checking its fingerprint, and remove each imported item individually. Revocation lists are not checked. Sceau is not affiliated with or endorsed by ANTS or BSI.
 Known limitations 
 German identity cards issued before 2 August 2021: the chip is reserved for authorities; Sceau cannot read it and says so. On newer cards, the address and place of birth cannot be read.
 German eID card for EU citizens: the chip holds no identity data; only its authenticity is verified.
 Italian CIE 3.0 identity cards from late 2017 to early 2018: Italy published an anomaly in their additional data; Sceau discards that data and verifies the rest of the document.
 Privacy 
 Only permission: NFC
 No data read from the chip is saved; memory is wiped when leaving the result or when the app goes to the background
 Screenshots and screen recordings are blocked throughout the app: they come out black, by design
 No ads, no trackers, no Google services
 Other 
 Four-page introduction on first launch, and a "What the chip contains" screen
 Interface in 45 languages
 Intended use 
Sceau is meant for checking your own document, or a document presented by its holder. Under the GDPR, the photo is biometric data when used for automated comparison: Sceau does not perform such comparison. The verdict does not tell whether the document has been reported lost or stolen.
Sceau does not read fingerprints or iris data, and does not scan the MRZ with the camera.
Free software under the GPL version 3 only.

fdroid:io.github.soichi11208.zinna.name: zinna-IME
fdroid:io.github.soichi11208.zinna.summary: Offline Japanese keyboard with mozc conversion, flick and qwerty
fdroid:io.github.soichi11208.zinna.description:
An open-source Japanese input method for Android.
Conversion is mozc — the engine behind Google Japanese Input's open-source release — compiled
natively into the app rather than reached over a network. The app declares no permissions at all,
INTERNET included, so nothing you type can leave the device even if a future dependency wanted it
to.
 Input 
* Flick, QWERTY, or kana on flick with the alphabet on QWERTY
* A second symbol plane for brackets, arrows, maths and typographic marks
* While a key is held, either a preview of what releasing will type or the full cross of four
 directions — and the symbol plane can always show the cross, since nobody memorises where ※ is
* Repeated presses of one key type the same character rather than cycling through it
 Conversion 
* Rule-based correction for mistyped readings, aware of where the keys actually sit on the flick
 layout: a slip within one key is treated as likelier than a hit on the neighbour
* Candidates that convert exactly what you typed are ranked ahead of guesses about what you have
 not finished typing
* Bundled dictionaries covering Niconico and Pixiv article titles, katakana loanwords with their
 English spellings, and Wikipedia headings
 Your data 
* The conversion history and your own dictionary are encrypted with a key held in the Android
 Keystore, which on devices with a secure element cannot be extracted at all
* Everything you cannot recreate — your dictionary, what the engine has learned, your settings —
 exports to a single file sealed under a passphrase you choose, and imports back on any device
* Clipboard history stays on the device and skips anything the source marked sensitive
 Appearance 
* Themes and keyboard layouts are plain JSON files you can replace
* Dark mode, Material You, a background image of your own, adjustable key height, pure black for
 OLED panels

 platforms, then Sigil is for you. You can use Sigil to format and package your books into an EPUB

 Table of Contents generator with multi-level heading support
 Metadata editor
 User interface translated into many languages
 Themeable icons
 Spell checking with default and user configurable dictionaries
 Full Regular Expression (PCRE) support for Find & Replace
 Supports import of EPUB and HTML files, images, and style sheets

flathub:io.github.bendik.Zodia.name: Zodia
flathub:io.github.bendik.Zodia.description:
Zodia calculates your natal chart and live planetary transits, and shows each
 aspect with interpretations drawn from a crowd-sourced pool. A curated baseline
 set is bundled in the app and always available offline, so you get meaningful
 readings from day one.
 Discover other Zodia users automatically. Nearby peers appear over mDNS on your
 local network; a global relay connects you to users anywhere on the internet.
 When two people exchange charts, shared aspects and synastry placements appear
 instantly alongside the community interpretations for those aspects.
 Connected peers can make direct voice calls. All communication is end-to-end
 encrypted over QUIC — no central server stores your birth data, chart, or

flathub:io.jor.mightymike.name: Mighty Mike
flathub:io.jor.mightymike.summary: High-Powered Action Rescue in a Toy Store Gone Mad!
flathub:io.jor.mightymike.description:
Toy Mart has closed for the evening. The clerks have long since turned off the cash registers, and the midnight janitor has left. Suddenly the store comes alive as dolls, action figures, and game pieces jump to their feet. Within moments cities are formed: in the Bargain Bin, race tracks become islands of action surrounded by a sea of on-looking toy robots. In the Clown Department thousands of insane clowns initiate a massive pie fight. Throughout all of the departments, life arises...
 Suddenly there is a commotion in the Doll Department! One of the cages in the Stuffed Animal Zoo has broken open – hundreds of Fuzzy Bunnies hop out of the cage and scatter. The Fuzzy Bunnies, with their limited intellect, do not realize the danger they are in. The new metropolis of Toy Mart can be a very dangerous place for Fuzzy Bunnies to wander alone, and without help they stand little chance of surviving until morning.
 The peaceful inhabitants of the Doll Department cry out for the Fuzzy Bunnies to return...but to no avail. What will they do? What will become of the Fuzzy Bunnies?
 “I WILL HELP YOU!” storms a deep, resonant voice from one of the shelves. A hush crawls over the crowd of Fuzzy onlookers. A large package tumbles from the shelf onto the floor and bursts open...and a figure emerges. Yes, it's Mighty Mike – the most powerful action figure money can buy!
 About this port: Mighty Mike was initially released as a Mac exclusive under the name “Power Pete” by Pangea Software in 1995. This port aims to provide the best way to experience the game today. This port was made and re-released under permission from Pangea Software, Inc.

KXStitch is a program that lets you create cross stitch patterns and charts. Patterns can be
 created from scratch on a user defined size of grid, which can be enlarged or reduced in size as
 your pattern progresses. Alternatively you can import images from many graphics file formats which
 will allow you to reduce the number of colors and to restrict the conversion to full stitches or
 optionally use fractional stitches. You may also use images as backgrounds allowing you to trace
 over them. These imported images can then be modified using the supplied tools to produce your
 final design.
 Features:
 Creation of new patterns
 Editing of existing patterns - KXStitch is also capable of reading PC Stitch files
 Use of various floss pallets, DMC, Anchor, Madeira
 Creation of custom palettes and colors
 Use of standard stitches
 Free use of backstitching
 Importing of various picture formats
 Printing of patterns and floss keys

fedora-packages:iwyu/iwyu.name: iwyu
fedora-packages:iwyu/iwyu.summary: C/C++ source files #include analyzer based on clang
fedora-packages:iwyu/iwyu.description: "Include what you use" means this: for every symbol (type, function, variable, or macro) that you use in foo.cc (or foo.cpp), either foo.cc or foo.h should include a .h file that exports the declaration of that symbol. (Similarly, for foo_test.cc, either foo_test.cc or foo.h should do the including.) Obviously symbols defined in foo.cc itself are excluded from this requirement. This puts us in a state where every file includes the headers it needs to declare the symbols that it uses. When every file includes what it uses, then it is possible to edit any file and remove unused headers, without fear of accidentally breaking the upwards dependencies of that file. It also becomes easy to automatically track and update dependencies in the source code.

fedora-packages:klt/klt.description: KLT is an implementation, in the C programming language, of a feature tracker for the computer vision community. The source code is in the public domain, available for both commercial and non-commercial use. The tracker is based on the early work of Lucas and Kanade, was developed fully by Tomasi and Kanade, and was explained clearly in the paper by Shi and Tomasi. Later, Tomasi proposed a slight modification which makes the computation symmetric with respect to the two images -- the resulting equation is derived in the unpublished note by myself. Briefly, good features are located by examining the minimum eigenvalue of each 2 by 2 gradient matrix, and features are tracked using a Newton-Raphson method of minimizing the difference between the two windows. Multi-resolution tracking allows for relatively large displacements between images. The affine computation that evaluates the consistency of features between non-consecutive frames was implemented by Thorsten Thormaehlen several years after the original code and documentation were written.

firefox-addons:994287.summary: Captures and translates subtitles using Google Translate directly from a webpage for online video services such as Netflix, HBO (free episodes only), YouTube and Amazon Video. Other similar HTML-based video and translate services can be configured.
firefox-addons:994287.description:

To configure other online video service you need set up the custom subtitles container selector value on the options page. Make sure that the parent container specified in the selector is always present in the page code, otherwise the extension icon will be inactive.
Sometimes Google Translate translates text in upper case from English to some languages (such as Russian) incorrectly. In this case, you may need using option "Convert to lower case before translating" (see add-on options).
Good luck!
Расширение Subs Translate извлекает субтитры непосредственно из HTML. Нажмите на иконку, чтобы открыть перевод в новой вкладке. Чтобы изменить целевой язык перевода (по умолчанию русский), замените «ru» внутри URL-адреса переводчика на нужный вам язык (de, fr, es и т. д.). 
Чтобы настроить другой сервис онлайн-видео, необходимо задать значение "Custom subtitles container selector" на странице параметров. При этом убедитесь, что родительский контейнер, указанный в селекторе, всегда присутствует в коде страницы, иначе иконка расширения будет неактивна.

firefox-addons:3109688.name: Fakeshop AI: Fake Shop Warnings
firefox-addons:3109688.summary: Warns you before you pay in a shop on our warning list. The matching runs in your browser.Warns you before you pay in a shop on our warning list. The matching runs in your browser.
firefox-addons:3109688.description:
Fakeshop AI warns you before you enter data or pay on a shop that is on our warning
list. The warning names our assessment, the source and the date of the list, and links
to the check report on fakeshop.ai .
The pages you visit stay with you
Every four hours the extension downloads a list of checksum prefixes and matches every
page you open against it, inside your browser. If a prefix matches, it requests the
checksums for that prefix: four bytes, from which your domain cannot be reconstructed.
The approach comes from Google Safe Browsing.
The domain itself is only sent to fakeshop.ai when you ask for it: “Load excerpt” in
the popup, “Load reasons and source” in the warning, “Open check report” or
“Report this shop”. The button says beforehand what is sent.
What you see
A warning over the page with the assessment danger or suspicious, each as a word and
a symbol, plus “Open check report” and “Continue anyway”.
A mark on the extension icon per tab: “!” for danger, “?” for suspicious.
In the popup the status of the current site and, on request, an excerpt from the
check report: assessment, source, date and key findings.
If you continued despite a warning, a slim notice as soon as you open the checkout
on the same domain. This is detected locally from the address.
No entry is not an all-clear
New fake shops are often not on any list yet. The popup says exactly that and offers
the shop check, which looks at the site itself: imprint, commercial register, domain
age, payment methods, trust seals.
You decide
Warnings and the checkout notice can be switched off, individual domains excluded
permanently. No sign-up, no account, no advertising. Our assessment is automated and
not a legally binding determination.
Privacy policy: https://fakeshop.ai/datenschutz

• Organize Google Docs into a "Docs" group

Discover, organize, and deepen all your personal and professional relationships with Mesh, a beautiful and intuitive contacts app, lightweight CRM, and more. Formerly known as Clay — same app, new name!
People make us laugh, challenge us to improve, support us when things are tough, and celebrate with us once they get better. But staying in touch with the people that matter thoughtfully is difficult. 
TRY MESH FOR FREE
Before Mesh, being thoughtful required relying on your memory as well as a mix of spreadsheets, notecards, address books, and other tools. In addition to being difficult to manage, this approach let important relationships, moments, and context fall through the cracks. That’s why we created Mesh—a stunning, intuitive, and private home for your relationships, built automatically from your email, calendar, address book, LinkedIn, Twitter, and iMessage. 
Mesh helps you show up informed by creating and automatically updating beautiful cards for each of your contacts with context such as profile photos, bios, education and work history, location, and social profiles. In addition, you can use powerful features such as natural-language search, dictation and note taking, reminders, birthday notifications, news articles about people you know, reconnection cadences, and more to deepen your relationships over time.
REMEMBER THE IMPORTANT THINGS
Mesh is the fastest and most powerful way to take notes before, during, and after a conversation with someone. Remember kids names, vacation itineraries, and that last article you read that you’ve been dying to share, all by writing a note on someone's card.
REACH OUT AT THE RIGHT MOMENT
Set a reminder for particular days—like a birthday or anniversary—or pick a reconnection cadence so you don’t lose touch. 
ORGANIZE YOUR RELATIONSHIPS
Dinner party faves? Book club? High school friends? Easily add people to groups so you can organize people however makes sense to you. Then, use those groups to make organizing events easier and faster.
SEARCH LIKE YOU THINK
You remember people in different ways—where you last met to catch up, when you last saw them, what you talked about. Just type what comes to mind and Mesh will find the right person or group of people based on your notes and their profile, all in milliseconds. It's the easiest, most powerful person search available anywhere.
STAY ON TOP OF THINGS
Never miss a beat with Home—a powerful, high-level view of all the updates from your entire network. Be the first to congratulate someone when they change jobs or when they're mentioned in thousands of top print and digital publications.
SHARE CONTACTS WITH YOUR TEAM
Mesh is the most beautiful, private, and seamless way to share contacts with your team — replace your CRM!
AND MUCH MORE
Business Cards: Easily import and digitize business card information.
Cleanup Contacts: Streamline and organize your contact list.
Cross-Device Sync and Cross-Platform: Access your contacts on any device.
Integrations: Connect with Gmail, Exchange, Office365, iCloud, Facebook, LinkedIn, Apple Contacts, Airtable, Pipedrive, Close, Affinity, Coda, Cardhop, and Rolodex
Birthday Reminders: Never miss an important date again.
Google Backup: Securely back up your contacts with Google.
Contacts+ Integration: With Mesh Pro, we're happy to import your contacts from Contacts+ via CSV
Automatic Contact Enrichment: Enrich contact details automatically (photos, social profiles, etc.).
Contact Deduplication: Merge duplicate contacts into a single comprehensive profile.
Contact Backup: Ensure your contacts are always safely backed up.
Widgets and Siri Shortcuts: First class support for Apple devices.
Unlimited contacts requires a Mesh Pro subscription. New users receive a 14 day trial of Mesh Pro, and can cancel anytime to be downgraded to Mesh Personal, which is free but has a limit of 1000 contacts.

apple-macos:6788401939.name: Knockoff: Shopping Filter
apple-macos:6788401939.description:
Amazon is flooded with trademark-squat "brands": random strings like SZHLUX, HORUSDY, and LATTOOK, registered at the USPTO purely to unlock Amazon Brand Registry. They sell commodity goods with no company, no warranty, and no reputation behind them.
Knockoff is a Safari extension that appraises every listing's brand right in your Amazon search results and hides, dims, or labels the junk, so what's left is brands with a reputation to lose. Works on iPhone, iPad, and Mac.
Featured in Fast Company, Gizmodo, 404 Media, PC Gamer, Yahoo, and Lifehacker.
HOW IT WORKS
• Every brand is checked against a curated register of established brands, refreshed daily.
• Unknown names are scored on the linguistic signature of pseudo-brands: all-caps squat-length strings, vanishing vowels, unpronounceable consonant runs.
• Your allowlist and blocklist override everything.
FEATURES
• Hide, dim, or label flagged listings, with a one-click reveal.
• Optionally hide Amazon's paid "Sponsored" listings too (off by default).
• Three filter levels: Relaxed, Standard, Strict.
• Trust or block any brand in one click, right from the results.
• One-click misclassification reporting that improves the shared lists for everyone.
PRIVATE BY DESIGN
Knockoff works only on Amazon pages. It has no access to your browsing history and never sees the other sites you visit. The brand appraisal runs locally on your device. No accounts, no profiles, nothing tied to you.
Two features send data. Both are on by default, and both can be switched off in settings: seller country sends seller IDs, so it can show where a seller is based; and Help pick US alternatives sends the product pages you open, so we know which products people want US alternatives for. A stored row records that a product was viewed N times, never who viewed it. Never sent: your searches, your orders, or anything you type into a page. Reports stay opt-in and anonymous. Full detail: knockoff.co/privacy
Free. Works on 23 Amazon marketplaces worldwide, including amazon.com, .ca, .co.uk, .de, .fr, .co.jp, .in, and .com.au.
To turn it on: enable Knockoff in Safari's Extensions settings and allow it on Amazon. Search as usual, and the junk brands drop out.
